African Union Welcomes UN Adoption of "Correct the Map" Resolution

2026-09-07 Vignikpo Akpéné, Afriquinfos African Union, Correct the Map, UN, Togo, Mercator, cartographic representation, Africa, equal-area projection, Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
Read the source article

Quick summary

The Chairperson of the African Union Commission welcomed the UN's adoption of the "Correct the Map" resolution, praising Togo's leadership in mobilizing African states to correct the Mercator projection's visual shrinking of Africa's true size.

Key takeaways

  • African Union Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf welcomed the UN adoption of the "Correct the Map" resolution
  • He praised Togo's leadership and President Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé for championing the initiative on behalf of Africa
  • The AU Commission noted the Mercator projection gives a "considerably reduced visual representation of the real size of the African continent"
  • The AU encourages international institutions, education systems, publishers, and digital actors to progressively adopt more faithful cartographic representations
  • Togo's diplomacy hailed the adoption as "a victory for accuracy" and pledged to focus on concrete implementation
  • The resolution passed with 164 votes in favor on September 4, 2026
